profile.name: TVS Motor Company Ltd
profile.what: India's third-largest two-wheeler maker and the world's third-largest by its own description: motorcycles (Apache, Raider, Ronin, HLX for exports, Sport, Radeon), scooters (Jupiter, Ntorq, Zest), the XL100 moped, electric scooters (iQube, Orbiter) and three-wheelers (King). Plants at Hosur, Mysuru and Nalagarh in India and Karawang (PT TVS) in Indonesia; owns Norton Motorcycles (UK); makes the BMW G 310 range for BMW Motorrad.

call.t: Commodity inflation ~3.5% of revenue in Q1 plus ~0.5% in Q2 (West Asia conflict: steel, aluminium, oil-linked parts); price increases ~1.5% in Q1 and ~0.5% in Q2.
Q2 industry: double-digit growth "minimum"; ICE slightly better than Q1, EV similar; watch Q3 for El Niño and the GST base effect; FY27 industry double-digit.
Capacity: 2W 6.8mn → 8.3mn and 3W 0.25mn → 0.42mn by Q4FY27; ~₹3,500 cr invested in new products and capacity. EV capacity 40k → 50k+ a month; EV 3W 20k → 30k.
EV contribution "becoming better and better quarter after quarter"; EV 2W penetration 10.6% in June; EV 3W penetration crossed 40%.
PLI ~0.6-0.7% of turnover; ~₹600 cr PLI receivable (annual claim), management "100%" confident of collection. AR FY26 government incentives ~₹1,100 cr (incl. export incentives).

Norton: ~₹2,000-2,500 cr invested in 4-5 years; Manx/Manx R built at Solihull, Atlas/Atlas GT at Hosur from June 2026; launched in UK, France, Italy, Germany, Spain, India; US later in 2026. No breakeven volume disclosed ("internal").
Dealer stock kept below 25-30 days; CARE upgraded the long-term rating from AA+ to AAA; NCRPS redemption due 1-Sep-2026 (analyst question).
TVS Credit: book ₹32,053 cr (+19%), Q1 PBT ₹283 cr (+16%), ~62,000 touch points, 2.6 crore customers.
Draft Delhi EV policy (proposal to stop ICE 2W sales from CY2028) raised by an analyst; management: "transitions we have to embrace".

q4fy26Guidance.t: FY27 industry: "good single-digit" growth (later raised to double-digit on the Q1 call); scooters, EV and premium to outgrow; economy motorcycles weakest.
FY27 capex ~₹3,500 cr (products ~₹2,000 cr + 1.5mn capacity ₹1,000 cr+ + R&D); investments in subsidiaries ~70% of FY26's ₹2,400 cr (FY26: mostly Norton, ~₹200 cr TVS Credit, ~₹300 cr Dubai).
Commodity inflation "3% to 5%" of revenue, unprecedented; ~35% offset by price increases at the time. No margin guidance ("pricing is a strategy").
FY26: EV revenue ~₹5,000 cr; Q4 PLI ~0.9% of revenue; Q4 IB revenue ₹2,999 cr, spares ₹1,122 cr; operating FCF ₹3,805 cr (+47%).

industryFromAR.t: FY26 domestic 2W wholesale +10.7% to 21.7mn, above the FY19 peak; scooters +18.5% to 8.11mn, motorcycles +6.6% to 13.5mn; premium motorcycles 1.83mn; e-2W retail 1.46mn (+27%), EV penetration 8.07% of all vehicles; CRISIL sees FY27 2W at ~29mn incl. exports (+7-9%).
FY25: domestic 2W wholesale 19.9mn vs 18.4mn (+8%), FY19 peak 21.2mn; e-2W retail 1.14mn (+22%), penetration 6.8%; India 2W exports 4.2mn (+22%).
TVS FY26: domestic 2W ICE 3.87mn (+19% vs industry +9%); 2W international +31% vs industry +12%; EV 2W 3.67 lakh (+35%), No.1 in EV 2W; 3W 2.2 lakh (+63% vs industry +28%).

norton.models: Manx, Manx R (1200cc V4), Atlas, Atlas GT (600cc twin) unveiled EICMA Nov-2025
norton.launch: UK, France, Italy, Germany, Spain, India in Q1FY27; US in summer FY27

ebike.note: Swiss E-Mobility Group renamed TVS EBike Company AG; SEMG Schweiz, Passion Velo and GO AG merged into it on 30-Jun-2025; European e-bike market has "excess inventory and excessive discounting" (AR FY26)

separation.t: At the AGM, Chairman Sudarshan Venu said TVS Motor is "evaluating alternatives including a possible separation of the financial services business", which "may, at an appropriate time in stages" happen; no structure or timeline given.

history.t: Emkay (18-Aug-2026): TVS Credit FY22-26 revenue CAGR 27%, PAT CAGR 66%.

ratings.t: AA+ from all three major agencies (FY26).

corporateActions.t: Swiss E-Mobility Group (Schweiz), Passion Velo and The GO Corporation merged into TVS EBike Company AG (formerly SEMG Holding).
NCLT approved the amalgamation of Sundaram Auto Components Ltd into TVS Motor (FY25 restated; ₹100 cr dividend from it moved to opening reserves).

Bonus of 4 listed 6% cumulative NCRPS of ₹10 for every equity share (190.03 cr NCRPS, ₹1,900.35 cr out of reserves), record date 25-Aug-2025, redeemable 1-Sep-2026; listed 10-Mar-2026. Carried as current borrowings (₹1,898.94 cr) at Mar-26.
Sudarshan Venu became Chairman & Managing Director; Venu Srinivasan Chairman Emeritus & MD; Sir Ralf Speth left the board on 22-Aug-2025.
Acquired 100% of Engines Engineering S.p.A. (Italy) via TVS Motor Singapore.
Invested ₹171.51 cr more in TVS Credit (stake 80.69% → 80.76%).
Sold the Rapido (Roppen Transportation) stake for ₹288 cr against ₹114 cr invested.
Interim dividend ₹12 per share (₹570 cr) for FY26.
CARE upgraded the long-term facility rating to AAA from AA+.
Bought a further 4.39% of TVS Credit from external holders for ₹711 cr (stake 85.15% fully diluted).
NCRPS redemption date (₹1,900 cr; ~₹40 per equity share).

accounting.t: Standalone other income FY26 −₹30.0 cr: interest ₹34.6 cr, PPE gains ₹14.9 cr, sale of investments ₹2.1 cr, other ₹6.2 cr, fair-value LOSS on investments ₹87.8 cr (FY25 loss ₹78.3 cr). Q1FY27 PBT includes a ₹150 cr fair-value GAIN.
Government grants in other operating revenue ₹973.6 cr in FY26 (₹488.5 cr in FY25): PLI plus export incentives; ~₹600 cr PLI receivable at the Q1 call.

Supplier finance: ₹946 cr of trade payables under supplier-finance arrangements at Mar-26 (₹1,236 cr at Mar-25); negative working capital (cash conversion cycle −56 days in FY26) partly rests on this.
Exceptional items FY26: ₹41.4 cr (one-time gratuity cost from the new Labour Codes).
Investments in subsidiaries carried at cost (₹11,299 cr equity + ₹50 cr preference at Mar-26); no impairment on TVS Motor Singapore despite cumulative Norton and e-bike losses.
